lesson: Treat line movement and money-vs-ticket splits as a tiebreaker only: when they are the main reason for a pick, require a 2.5+ point model edge or pass.

lesson: In the NBA, when the main case for a side is the other team's injuries or a tired/travel spot, require a 2.5+ point model edge at any spread size, and don't use those plays as the pick of the day.
evidence: Nov 8 review and week of Nov 2-8: NBA injury/spot fades went about 3-6 ATS (CLE, DAL, MEM twice, DET, NOP lost), mostly on 1-2 pt edges, and all five POTD losses were NBA spot plays. POTD part held: the SAS POTD was a healthy-favorite read and won. Nov 10: PHX -3.5 (kept the tired Suns rather than a 1.5-pt LAC fade) won by 23; now 1-1. lesson: Treat a model edge of 3+ points as a warning, not confidence: recheck for news, injuries or info the market has that the model missed; if no clear specific reason the line is wrong, shrink the edge to under 2 or flip/pass, and never make a 3+ edge the pick of the day just for its size.
evidence: Nov 2-8 board by edge size: under 1 pt 14-9 (61%), 1-2 pts 45-31 (59%), 2-3 pts 19-17 (53%), 3+ pts 8-8 (50%). The bigger the disagreement with the market, the more often the market was right. Nov 9 (untagged, not counted): ATL +2.5 on a 3.0-pt edge lost by 10 as a bad read. Nov 11 first tagged day: 4-2 (SJU, HOU, UCLA, USC covered after the model's 3+ edges toward the dogs were shrunk/flipped; ARK and NEB fell short). Avg CLV +0.2 on 6 tagged games. lesson: When the line moves against our side even though most bets are on it (reverse line movement), pass or switch unless the model edge is 2.5+ points.
evidence: Nov 10 review: PHI +1.5 on a 2-pt edge lost by 22 after the line flipped from PHI -1.5 to BOS -1.5 with the money on Philly; the note flagged the warning and took it anyway. It flipped IND-WAS to WAS +3.5 off a 2-pt drop with 54% of bets on IND (IND won by 13, line was right), and kept MEM +3.5 (close loss, DEN by 5). Both were split picks (fav ML, dog ATS); worth watching whether it should yield to L008 when they conflict. Nov 14 recount: 0-2 (0%), 95% range 0-66%, p=1.00, avg CLV +0.5 on 2, 2/50 picks needed.

lesson: Early in the season (roughly the first 10-15 games in NBA/CBB, first 4-5 weeks in NFL/CFB), weight a team's track record - last season's results, multi-year program strength, preseason power ratings, coaching and returning core - more than its small current-season sample. Don't overreact to a historically strong team's slow start or a historically weak team's hot start. Still don't double count: brand-name teams are often already overpriced by public money, so only lean on history where the line looks driven by the small sample.
evidence: Added at Isaac's request: early-season records are mostly noise, so long-run team strength may be underweighted when the line chases a few results. Nov 14 recount: No graded picks yet; 0/50 picks needed.

lesson: Adjust records and margins for strength of schedule: a team with a great record built mostly against weak opponents is worse than it looks, and a team with a so-so record against a tough schedule is better than it looks. Use opponent-adjusted ratings (KenPom/Torvik/net rating vs. quality opponents, SOS rank) instead of raw record, especially when the line seems to be pricing the raw record.
evidence: Added at Isaac's request: raw records against weak schedules can make teams look better than they are. Related to L013 (early season / team history). Nov 12 first tagged pick: TOR +10.5 lost by the hook (PHI by 11) at +3 CLV; now 0-1. Nov 14 recount: 0-1 (0%), 95% range 0-79%, p=1.00, avg CLV +3.0 on 1, 1/50 picks needed.

lesson: In CBB, don't use L011 to flip a model underdog lean onto the favorite; keep the model's dog side when its edge is under 2 points, or pass, and save the L011 flip for the NBA/NFL.
evidence: Nov 12 review: L011 flips in CBB are 1-5 ATS (FLA, IOWA, DUKE, CREI, BYU lost; USC won) while its NBA flips are 2-0. BYU -23.5 lost by 8.5 when the raw BYU -16.5 number was closer. Nov 14 recount: No graded picks yet; 0/50 picks needed.

lesson: In CBB games with a spread of 20+, when the rating line (Torvik/KenPom) is 5+ points short of the favorite's number, don't let L010 shrink the edge into laying the full chalk; take the dog only if L004's bar and a specific reason are met, otherwise pass.
evidence: Nov 13 review: nine 25+ CBB favorites laid against Torvik dog leans of 8-15 pts went 2-7 ATS (raw dog side 7-2); same shape as ARK and NEB on Nov 11 and BYU on Nov 12. Conflicts between L004/L010 and the ratings; 0/50 picks needed.
